label: East Friesian

names.text: Opened the Wikipedia article. The German and Dutch names and the name Fries Melkschaap are as the article gives them. The known record's names were checked against it.

about.text: A dairy sheep from Frisia, on the border of the north-east Netherlands and north-west Germany. It is used purebred and in crosses to raise milk yield and lambs born per ewe.

sources.text: Taken from the article's lead and its section on use. The article says it is a dairy breed, used purebred or as a crossing breed to improve milk yield and lambs born per ewe.

origin.place: Frisia: parts of the north-east Netherlands and north-west Germany

sources.text: Taken from the article's lead. It gives no date of formation.

The article says the breed produces roughly 300 to 600 litres of milk over a 200- to 300-day lactation. The figures here are those litres taken as kg at about 1.03 kg per litre (300 x 1.03 = 309, rounded to 310; 600 x 1.03 = 618, rounded to 620). That conversion is worked out, not read off the page; the schema has no estimated flag on yield, so the working here is the only marker. The article gives no year for these figures.
The article calls it a dairy breed.

The article's infobox gives DAD-IS (2023) as at risk, endangered-maintained, and FAO (2007) as not at risk. The DAD-IS figure is used here, as the article reports it. The DAD-IS breed page itself was not opened.

facts.v: Some individual animals have reportedly given 900 litres, counting milk suckled by lambs and machine milking.

sources.text: Taken from the article's section on milk yield. The article calls it a reported figure.

gaps: Breed population count: the only figure on the article is an unlabelled FAO (2007) value of 147, which was not used. Date of formation. Fat, protein, lactose and solids percentages: searches returned only figures for crossbred or mixed flocks, which were not used. Year for the yield figure. The DAD-IS breed page was not opened.
